questions.stem: A retailer most likely reports which inventory category?
questions.explanation: Merchandisers (wholesalers, retailers) buy finished goods ready for sale — one category only. Raw materials and WIP belong to manufacturers.
questions.kr: 유통업자(도·소매)는 판매용 완제품만 보유 — 한 범주. 원재료·재공품은 제조업.

questions.stem: Work-in-progress inventory is best described as goods that:

choices.A: have been purchased but not received
choices.B: have started conversion but are not yet ready for sale

questions.explanation: WIP has started the conversion process from raw materials but is not yet finished goods.
questions.kr: 재공품 = 원재료에서 전환을 시작했지만 아직 완제품이 아닌 것.

questions.stem: A manufacturer reports only total inventory on its balance sheet. It most likely must:

choices.A: disclose raw materials, WIP and finished goods in a footnote

questions.explanation: If only the total is on the face, the three category amounts must be disclosed in a footnote.
questions.kr: 재무상태표에 총액만 표시하면 세 범주 금액을 주석에 공시.

questions.stem: Which method is permitted under US GAAP but NOT under IFRS?
questions.explanation: Same three everywhere (specific ID, FIFO, weighted average); LIFO is US GAAP only.
questions.kr: 공통 3개(개별법·FIFO·가중평균), LIFO는 US GAAP만.

questions.stem: The choice of inventory valuation method affects:

choices.A: the total cost of goods available for sale
choices.B: the allocation of goods available between ending inventory and cost of sales
choices.C: neither inventory nor cost of sales

questions.explanation: The method doesn't change the pool (beginning inventory + purchases); it only splits it between ending inventory and COGS.
questions.kr: 방법은 판매가능상품 총액이 아니라 기말재고와 매출원가 사이의 '배분'을 바꿈.

questions.stem: Raw materials 400; direct labour 250; variable production overhead 60; fixed production overhead 40; freight-in on materials 20; abnormal waste 15; storage of finished goods 10; selling costs 30. The amount capitalised into inventory is closest to:
questions.explanation: IN: 400 + 250 + 60 + 40 + 20 = 770 (fixed overhead and freight-in included). OUT: abnormal waste, finished-goods storage, selling. B drops fixed overhead or freight; C adds abnormal waste.
questions.kr: 포함: 400 + 250 + 60 + 40 + 20 = 770(고정제조간접비·매입운임 포함). 제외: 비정상 손실, 완제품 보관, 판매비. C는 비정상 손실 포함.

questions.stem: Under both IFRS and US GAAP, which cost is LEAST likely included in inventory?

choices.C: Storage of finished goods not required by production

questions.explanation: Least-likely → T/F. Freight-in (in), fixed production overhead (in). Storage of finished goods (not part of production) is expensed → answer.
questions.kr: least likely → T/F. 매입운임(포함), 고정제조간접비(포함). 생산에 필요 없는 완제품 보관비는 비용 → 정답.

questions.stem: A company capitalises administrative overhead into inventory. Compared with correct treatment, in the current period it most likely reports:
questions.explanation: Wrongly capitalising defers the expense → profit AND inventory both overstated.
questions.kr: 잘못 자본화 → 비용 이연 → 이익과 재고 '모두' 과대.

questions.stem: A trade discount received on raw materials most likely:
questions.explanation: Trade discounts, rebates and similar items reduce the cost of purchase.
questions.kr: 매입할인·리베이트는 매입원가를 감소시킴.

questions.stem: Storage costs are included in the cost of inventory when:

choices.B: storage is required as part of the production process

questions.explanation: Storage is excluded UNLESS required by production (e.g., ageing whisky or wine).
questions.kr: 보관비는 생산 과정에 필요한 경우(위스키 숙성 등)만 포함.

questions.stem: The specific identification method is most appropriate for:

choices.B: precious gemstones that are uniquely identifiable

questions.explanation: Specific ID suits items not ordinarily interchangeable, segregated projects, and expensive unique goods. Interchangeable items use FIFO/average/LIFO assumptions.
questions.kr: 개별법은 상호 대체 불가·고가·고유 식별 가능 품목(보석)에 적합.

questions.stem: In rising prices, a company using FIFO rather than LIFO most likely reports:

choices.A: higher COGS and lower ending inventory
choices.B: lower COGS and higher ending inventory

questions.explanation: FIFO sends the oldest (cheapest) costs to COGS and leaves the newest (dearest) in inventory.
questions.kr: FIFO는 오래된(싼) 원가를 매출원가로, 최신(비싼) 원가를 재고로.

questions.stem: In falling prices, which method gives the highest ending inventory?
questions.explanation: LIFO ending inventory holds the OLDEST costs — which are the HIGHEST when prices fall.
questions.kr: LIFO 기말재고 = 가장 오래된 원가 — 가격 하락기엔 가장 높음.

questions.stem: If inventory costs are constant, the choice of inventory method most likely:
questions.explanation: With constant prices all methods give nearly the same COGS and ending inventory.
questions.kr: 가격 불변이면 모든 방법의 결과가 거의 같음.

questions.stem: Under IFRS, a company must use:

choices.A: the same method for all inventory
choices.B: the same method for items of similar nature and use

questions.explanation: Same method for items of SIMILAR NATURE AND USE; different nature or use may justify a different method.
questions.kr: 성격·용도가 비슷한 항목엔 같은 방법; 다르면 다른 방법 가능.

questions.stem: Beginning inventory 50 units @ $8; purchases 100 @ $10 and 50 @ $12; 120 units sold. FIFO ending inventory is closest to:
questions.explanation: Units left = 200 − 120 = 80. FIFO EI = newest layers: 50 × 12 + 30 × 10 = 600 + 300 = 900. Check: FIFO COGS = 2,000 − 900 = 1,100.

questions.stem: Using Q16's data, LIFO cost of goods sold is closest to:
Using Q16's data, weighted average cost per unit is closest to:
questions.explanation: Total cost 400 + 1,000 + 600 = 2,000 ÷ total units 200 = $10.00. Weight by units (incl. beginning inventory), not a simple average of prices (8, 10, 12 → also 10 here, but don't rely on it).
questions.kr: 총원가 2,000 ÷ 총수량 200 = 10.00. 기초재고 포함, 수량 가중.

questions.stem: With declining inventory costs, which method most likely reports the highest gross profit?
questions.explanation: Falling prices: LIFO's COGS carries the newest (cheapest) costs → lowest COGS → highest gross profit (GSI: 75,600).
questions.kr: 가격 하락: LIFO 매출원가 = 최신(가장 싼) → 매출원가 최저 → 매출총이익 최고(GSI 75,600).

questions.stem: In a company's first year, total cost of goods available for sale under FIFO vs LIFO is:
questions.explanation: No beginning inventory → goods available = purchases, identical under every method.
questions.kr: 기초재고 없음 → 판매가능상품 = 매입액, 모든 방법 동일.

questions.stem: After the first year, cost of goods available typically differs across methods because:
questions.explanation: Each method's prior ending inventory becomes its beginning inventory — those differ.
questions.kr: 각 방법의 전기 기말재고(= 당기 기초)가 다름.

questions.stem: First year. Purchases: 40 @ $50, then 60 @ $45, then 50 @ $40. 110 units sold. LIFO ending inventory is closest to:
questions.explanation: Units left 150 − 110 = 40. LIFO EI = OLDEST layer: 40 × 50 = 2,000. A (1,600) is FIFO's EI (40 × 40).
questions.kr: 남은 40. LIFO 기말 = 가장 오래된 층: 40×50 = 2,000. A는 FIFO(40×40).

questions.stem: Using Q22's data, FIFO cost of goods sold is closest to:
Which method's cost of sales always falls between FIFO and LIFO?
questions.explanation: Weighted average is always between; specific ID depends on which units were physically sold.
questions.kr: 가중평균은 항상 중간; 개별법은 실제 판매 품목에 따라 다름.

questions.stem: The allocation of goods available is the same under periodic and perpetual systems for:
questions.explanation: Specific ID and FIFO: same. Weighted average (moving vs year-end average) and LIFO: generally different.
questions.kr: 개별법·FIFO 동일. 가중평균(이동 vs 연말)·LIFO는 대체로 다름.

questions.stem: Analysts typically don't adjust when comparing a FIFO company with a weighted-average company because:

choices.B: perpetual systems dominate and the two give similar results under them
choices.C: the two give identical results under any system

questions.explanation: Under perpetual systems FIFO and (moving) weighted average are similar; disclosure is limited. Under periodic they can differ a lot, so C is false.
questions.kr: 영구재고법에서는 FIFO와 이동평균이 비슷하고 공시가 제한적. 실지재고법에선 크게 다를 수 있어 C 거짓.

questions.stem: With rising costs and stable quantities, LIFO rather than FIFO most likely gives:

choices.A: lower net income and lower operating cash flow
choices.B: lower net income and higher operating cash flow
choices.C: higher net income and higher operating cash flow

questions.explanation: LIFO lowers income → lower taxes paid → HIGHER operating cash flow. COGS itself isn't cash; taxes are.
questions.kr: LIFO는 이익 ↓ → 세금 ↓ → 영업현금흐름 '증가'. 매출원가는 현금 아님, 세금은 현금.

questions.stem: Under the same conditions, LIFO compared with FIFO results in:
questions.explanation: LIFO inventory (oldest, cheapest costs) is lower → current assets, working capital and total assets lower.
questions.kr: LIFO 재고(싼 옛 원가) ↓ → 유동자산·운전자본·총자산 ↓.

questions.stem: Under a periodic system, cost of sales is determined as:

choices.A: the running total at each sale

questions.explanation: Periodic: COGS = goods available − ending inventory (often from a physical count).
questions.kr: 실지재고법: 매출원가 = 판매가능 − 기말(실사).

questions.stem: Buy 100 @ $10; sell 80; buy 100 @ $12; sell 60. Perpetual LIFO ending inventory is closest to:
questions.explanation: After sale 1: 20 @ 10. Buy → 20 @ 10 + 100 @ 12. Sale 2 takes 60 from the newest (12) → 20 @ 10 + 40 @ 12 = 200 + 480 = 680. B is periodic LIFO.
questions.kr: 1차 판매 후 20@10. 매입 후 판매 60은 최신(12)에서 → 20@10 + 40@12 = 680. B는 실지재고 LIFO.

questions.stem: Using Q30's data, periodic LIFO ending inventory is closest to:
questions.explanation: Periodic: 200 units available, 140 sold, 60 left — valued at the OLDEST costs: 60 × 10 = 600.
questions.kr: 실지재고: 200개 중 140 판매, 60개를 가장 오래된 원가로: 600.

questions.stem: Which method's balance-sheet inventory most closely reflects current replacement value?
questions.explanation: FIFO ending inventory = most recent purchases. LIFO = current values on the INCOME statement.
questions.kr: FIFO 기말재고 = 최근 매입. LIFO는 손익계산서에 현행가치.

questions.stem: LIFO is most likely to give a cost of sales that:

choices.A: reflects current replacement value more closely than FIFO
choices.C: equals FIFO cost of sales during inflation

questions.explanation: LIFO COGS = most recent costs → closest to current replacement value. B describes LIFO ending inventory.
questions.kr: LIFO 매출원가 = 최신 원가. B는 LIFO 기말재고.

questions.stem: With declining unit costs and stable quantities, FIFO compared with LIFO reports:
questions.explanation: Declining costs: FIFO puts the older, HIGHER costs into COGS → lower gross profit and pre-tax income; FIFO EI holds the newest (lowest) costs.
questions.kr: 원가 하락: FIFO는 오래된 '높은' 원가를 매출원가로 → 매출총이익 ↓, 기말재고는 최신(낮은) 원가.

questions.stem: Two identical companies differ only in LIFO vs FIFO. During inflation the LIFO company reports higher inventory turnover. This most likely indicates:

choices.A: the LIFO company manages inventory more efficiently
choices.B: an accounting effect of LIFO carrying amounts unaffected by inflation
choices.C: the LIFO company holds fewer units

questions.explanation: Same units, same prices — turnover is higher only because LIFO inventory stays at old costs. The curriculum calls the 'better management' reading deceptive.
questions.kr: 수량·가격 동일 — LIFO 재고가 옛 원가에 머물러 회전율이 높을 뿐. '관리가 더 효율적'은 착시.

questions.stem: In Example 4, Company L's gross margin is constant because:

choices.B: sales and cost of sales both rise at the inflation rate

questions.explanation: LIFO COGS = current-year purchases, rising with inflation just like sales → constant margin.
questions.kr: LIFO 매출원가 = 당해 매입, 매출과 같은 인플레이션율로 상승 → 이익률 일정.

questions.stem: During inflation, a LIFO company sells more units than it buys. Compared with no liquidation, its gross margin is most likely:

choices.A: higher, because old low-cost layers flow into COGS

questions.explanation: LIFO liquidation pushes old, cheap layers into COGS at current selling prices → higher (one-time) gross margin.
questions.kr: LIFO 청산 → 오래된 싼 원가가 매출원가로 → 일회성 이익률 상승.

questions.stem: In Example 4, Company F's Year 3 inventory turnover (COGS ÷ ending inventory) is closest to:
The LIFO reserve is best described as:

choices.C: the cumulative tax saved by LIFO

questions.explanation: LIFO reserve = FIFO inventory − LIFO inventory (positive in rising prices). Tax saved ≈ reserve × t.
questions.kr: LIFO 충당금 = FIFO 재고 − LIFO 재고. 절세액 ≈ 충당금 × 세율.

questions.stem: A LIFO company reports inventory of $500m; its LIFO reserve was $80m at the start of the year and $95m at the end. FIFO inventory is closest to:
questions.explanation: Balance sheet uses the reserve's LEVEL: 500 + 95 = 595. A adds only the change (trap 2); B uses the opening reserve.
questions.kr: 재무상태표는 충당금 '잔액': 500 + 95 = 595. A는 변동분만 더함.

questions.stem: Using Q40's data and LIFO COGS of $2,000m, FIFO COGS is closest to:
questions.explanation: Income statement uses the reserve's CHANGE: 2,000 − (95 − 80) = 1,985. B subtracts the level (trap 1); C has the wrong sign.
questions.kr: 손익계산서는 충당금 '변동': 2,000 − 15 = 1,985. B는 잔액 차감, C는 부호 반대.

questions.stem: A LIFO company's reserve fell from $60m to $45m. Relative to LIFO COGS, FIFO COGS is:
questions.explanation: Reserve DECREASED by 15 → FIFO COGS = LIFO COGS + 15 (higher). A falling reserve usually means a LIFO liquidation or falling prices.
questions.kr: 충당금 15 '감소' → FIFO 매출원가 = LIFO + 15(더 높음). 감소는 보통 LIFO 청산·가격 하락.

questions.stem: With rising costs, a company using LIFO rather than FIFO most likely reports:
questions.explanation: LIFO → lower retained earnings → lower equity → HIGHER D/E. Current ratio lower (inventory ↓), profitability lower.
questions.kr: LIFO → 이익잉여금 ↓ → 자본 ↓ → 부채비율 ↑. 유동비율 ↓, 수익성 ↓.

questions.stem: Under the LIFO conformity rule, a US company that uses LIFO for tax must:

choices.A: also use LIFO for financial reporting
choices.B: disclose FIFO income on the face
choices.C: switch to FIFO when prices fall

questions.explanation: LIFO for tax ⇒ LIFO for financial reporting.
questions.kr: 세무상 LIFO ⇒ 재무보고도 LIFO.

questions.concept: Why not LIFO when costs fall
questions.stem: When inventory costs are falling, a company is least likely to adopt LIFO because LIFO would result in:

choices.B: higher taxable income and income taxes

questions.explanation: Falling costs: LIFO COGS = newest (cheapest) → lower COGS → higher taxable income and taxes. A and C are the rising-cost effects.
questions.kr: 원가 하락: LIFO 매출원가 ↓ → 과세소득·세금 ↑. A·C는 상승기 효과.

questions.stem: Compared with FIFO, LIFO during rising costs results in shareholders' equity that is:
questions.explanation: Cumulative lower net income → lower retained earnings → lower equity.
questions.kr: 누적 순이익 ↓ → 이익잉여금 ↓ → 자본 ↓.

questions.stem: Which disclosure most likely indicates a LIFO liquidation?

choices.A: An increase in the LIFO reserve
choices.B: A decrease in the LIFO reserve from the prior period

questions.explanation: A declining LIFO reserve may indicate a liquidation (old layers sold off).
questions.kr: LIFO 충당금 감소 → 청산 가능성.

questions.stem: Gross profit created by a LIFO liquidation during rising costs is best described as:
questions.explanation: Old cheap layers can be liquidated only once — inventory profits are one-time and unsustainable.
questions.kr: 옛 저가층은 한 번만 청산 가능 — 일회성, 지속 불가.

questions.stem: Current purchase cost is $50/unit. A LIFO company liquidates 4,000 units from a layer carried at $32. Gross profit attributable to the liquidation is closest to:
questions.explanation: 4,000 × (50 − 32) = 72,000. B is the old layer's cost (4,000 × 32); C is current cost (4,000 × 50).

questions.stem: A LIFO company's reserve increased by $100m; tax rate 25%. Converting to FIFO, net income changes by:
questions.explanation: FIFO COGS lower by 100 → pre-tax +100 → NI + 100 × (1 − 0.25) = +75.
questions.kr: FIFO 매출원가 100 ↓ → 세전 +100 → 순이익 +75.

questions.stem: LIFO reserve at year-end $400m; tax 30%. Using the tax-adjusted approach, the FIFO adjustment to equity is closest to:
questions.explanation: Equity + reserve × (1 − t) = 400 × 0.7 = 280; the 120 becomes a deferred tax liability. A is the no-tax alternative.
questions.kr: 자본 + 400 × 0.7 = 280, 120은 이연법인세부채. A는 세금 무시 방식.

questions.stem: When restating a LIFO balance sheet to FIFO for analysis (no actual change), the tax on the reserve is most appropriately shown as:
questions.explanation: No conversion actually happens, so no cash is paid — show a deferred tax liability (Caterpillar: +1,924 inventory = +1,214 equity + 710 DTL).
questions.kr: 실제 전환이 아니므로 현금 지급 없음 — 이연법인세부채로 표시.

questions.stem: A LIFO company's reserve fell during the year. Converting to FIFO, operating cash flow (through taxes) would be:
questions.explanation: Falling reserve → FIFO COGS HIGHER → lower taxable income → less tax → FIFO CFO HIGHER. The usual 'LIFO → higher CFO' assumes a rising reserve (Caterpillar Q4).
questions.kr: 충당금 감소 → FIFO 매출원가 ↑ → 세금 ↓ → FIFO 영업현금 ↑. 통상 결론은 충당금 증가 가정.

questions.stem: Management could inflate gross profit at year-end under LIFO by:

choices.B: deliberately reducing quantities so old layers are liquidated

questions.explanation: Deliberately running inventory down liquidates old cheap layers into COGS → higher gross profit. A would add new expensive layers.
questions.kr: 의도적 재고 축소 → 옛 저가층 청산 → 매출총이익 ↑. A는 비싼 신규층 추가.

questions.stem: Under IFRS, a change in inventory method is acceptable only if it:

choices.B: results in reliable and more relevant information

questions.explanation: IFRS: only if reliable and more relevant information results.
questions.kr: IFRS: 신뢰성 있고 더 목적적합한 정보를 제공할 때만.

questions.stem: Under US GAAP, a company changing from FIFO to LIFO most likely:

choices.B: applies the change prospectively, with the FIFO carrying amount becoming the first LIFO layer
choices.C: records the cumulative effect in current net income

questions.explanation: The exception: a change TO LIFO is prospective; the old carrying amount becomes the initial LIFO layer.
questions.kr: 예외: LIFO로의 변경은 전진 적용; 기존 장부가가 최초 LIFO층.

questions.stem: Under US GAAP, a change from LIFO to weighted average must be applied:
questions.explanation: Leaving LIFO → look back (retrospective). Joining LIFO → look forward (prospective).
questions.kr: LIFO 이탈 → 소급, LIFO 도입 → 전진.

questions.stem: A company changes its inventory method in 2018 and presents 2016–2018. The cumulative effect on periods before 2016 is recorded in:

choices.B: the opening 2016 balance of retained earnings

questions.explanation: Retrospective: restate 2016–2017; earlier effects go to the opening equity balance of the earliest period presented.
questions.kr: 소급: 2016–17 재작성, 이전 효과는 최초 표시기간 기초 이익잉여금.

questions.stem: Compared with IFRS, US GAAP additionally requires a company changing its inventory method to:

choices.B: explain why the new method is superior and preferable

questions.explanation: US GAAP: thoroughly explain why the new method is preferable.
questions.kr: US GAAP: 새 방법이 더 바람직한 이유를 충분히 설명.

questions.stem: In rising costs, a company switches from FIFO to LIFO citing 'better matching.' The unstated purpose is most likely to:
questions.explanation: To LIFO in rising costs → higher COGS → lower taxes. (From LIFO → higher profits.)
questions.kr: 상승기 LIFO 전환 → 매출원가 ↑ → 세금 ↓.

questions.stem: Under IFRS, inventory cost €800k; NRV €720k. Next year NRV rises to €850k. The reversal recognised next year is closest to:
questions.explanation: Write-down 80; the reversal is capped at the original write-down → 80 (carrying amount back to cost 800, never above).
questions.kr: 감액 80; 환입은 원래 감액액까지 → 80(원가 800 초과 불가).

questions.stem: US GAAP (LIFO): cost $100; NRV $95; NRV less normal margin $80; replacement cost $75. Inventory is carried at:
questions.explanation: Market = middle of {75, 95, 80} = 80 (replacement 75 is below the floor). Lower of cost (100) and market (80) = 80.
questions.kr: 시가 = {75, 95, 80}의 중간값 = 80(대체원가가 하한 미만). 원가 100과 비교 → 80.

questions.stem: Same as Q62 but replacement cost is $98. Inventory is carried at:
questions.explanation: Replacement 98 > ceiling NRV 95 → market = 95. Lower of cost (100) and market (95) = 95.
questions.kr: 대체원가 98 > 상한 95 → 시가 95. 원가 100과 비교 → 95.

questions.stem: Under IFRS, a reversal of an inventory write-down is recognised as:

choices.B: a reduction in cost of sales

questions.explanation: IFRS reversal = reduction in cost of sales.
questions.kr: IFRS 환입 = 매출원가 감소.

questions.stem: An inventory write-down will most likely:
questions.explanation: Smaller inventory denominator → turnover UP. Profitability, liquidity (current ratio) and solvency go down.
questions.kr: 재고(분모) ↓ → 회전율 '상승'. 수익성·유동성·안정성은 하락.

questions.stem: A producer of agricultural products measures inventory at fair value less costs to sell. An increase in value above cost is:
questions.explanation: Outside IAS 2: changes in value (up or down) go to profit or loss, with no cost cap.
questions.kr: IAS 2 적용 제외: 가치 변동(증감)은 당기손익, 원가 상한 없음.

questions.stem: With rising costs, write-downs are LEAST likely for a company using:
questions.explanation: LIFO inventory already carries the oldest, lowest costs → conservatively stated → write-downs less likely and smaller.
questions.kr: LIFO 재고는 이미 가장 낮은 옛 원가 → 감액 가능성 낮음.

questions.stem: A company's inventory obsolescence allowance rose from 400 to 460. Assuming changes go through cost of sales, removing the allowance changes cost of sales by:
questions.explanation: The 60 increase was charged to COGS; removing it lowers COGS by 60. Income statement uses the CHANGE, not the level (C).
questions.kr: 증가분 60이 매출원가에 포함 → 제거 시 −60. 손익은 '변동', 잔액(C) 아님.

questions.stem: Companies may be reluctant to record write-downs, especially under US GAAP, because:

choices.B: write-downs reduce key ratios and cannot be reversed

questions.explanation: Ratios suffer and, under US GAAP, the write-down can never be reversed.
questions.kr: 비율 악화 + US GAAP는 환입 불가.

questions.stem: Cost of sales 1,200; beginning inventory 180; ending inventory 220. Inventory turnover (average inventory) is closest to:
questions.explanation: Average inventory = (180 + 220)/2 = 200; 1,200 / 200 = 6.0. A uses ending (5.45); C uses beginning.

questions.stem: Using Q70's data, days of inventory on hand based on ENDING inventory is closest to:
questions.explanation: Ending basis: turnover = 1,200 / 220 = 5.45 → 365 / 5.45 = 66.9 days. A uses the average basis (365/6.0).

questions.stem: Inventory turnover is well above the industry average but sales growth is well below it. The most likely explanation is:
questions.explanation: High turnover + slower sales growth → too little inventory (lost sales / stock-outs).
questions.kr: 높은 회전율 + 낮은 매출성장 → 재고 부족.

questions.stem: High turnover with minimal write-downs and sales growth at or above the industry most likely indicates:
questions.explanation: The supporting evidence for efficiency: few write-downs + sales growth ≥ industry.
questions.kr: 효율 근거: 감액 적음 + 매출성장 ≥ 업계.

questions.stem: A low inventory turnover relative to industry most likely indicates:
questions.explanation: Low turnover / high days → slow-moving or obsolete inventory.
questions.kr: 낮은 회전율 → 진부·저회전 재고.

questions.stem: Which disclosure is required under IFRS but NOT under US GAAP?

choices.B: The amount of any reversal of a write-down
choices.C: The carrying amount pledged as security

questions.explanation: US GAAP prohibits reversals, so reversal disclosures (items f, g) don't apply.
questions.kr: US GAAP는 환입 금지 → 환입 공시 해당 없음.

questions.stem: US GAAP, but not IFRS, requires disclosure of:

choices.B: inventories at fair value less costs to sell

questions.explanation: LIFO exists only under US GAAP, so only US GAAP requires LIFO-liquidation income disclosure (plus significant estimates).
questions.kr: LIFO는 US GAAP만 → LIFO 청산이익 공시도 US GAAP만.

questions.stem: Compared with a seller of staples, a seller of luxury products most likely has:
questions.explanation: Luxury: high margins, much lower turnover.
questions.kr: 명품: 높은 이익률, 낮은 회전율.

questions.stem: A manufacturer's raw materials and WIP rise significantly due to higher volumes. This most likely signals:
questions.explanation: Building inputs in volume → expects more demand.
questions.kr: 투입재 수량 증가 → 수요 증가 예상.

questions.stem: Finished goods rise substantially while raw materials and WIP decline. This most likely signals:

choices.B: declining demand and a possible future write-down

questions.explanation: Unsold finished goods piling up while production inputs are cut → falling demand.
questions.kr: 완제품 적체 + 투입 축소 → 수요 감소.

questions.stem: Finished goods grow 15% while sales grow 3%. The analyst should be most concerned about:
questions.explanation: Inventory outgrowing sales → mark-downs or obsolescence write-downs ahead.
questions.kr: 재고가 매출보다 빠르게 증가 → 가격인하·감액 우려.

questions.stem: To compare a US LIFO company with an IFRS company, an analyst should most appropriately:

choices.A: restate the IFRS company to LIFO
choices.B: restate the LIFO company to FIFO

questions.explanation: IFRS forbids LIFO; restate the LIFO company to FIFO using the reserve.
questions.kr: IFRS는 LIFO 금지 → LIFO 회사를 FIFO로 재작성.

questions.stem: LIFO company: FIFO net income 500; equity 10,000 (end) and 9,600 (start); LIFO reserve 1,000 (end) and 800 (start); tax 25%. FIFO ROE (average equity) is closest to:
questions.explanation: FIFO equity end = 10,000 + 1,000 × 0.75 = 10,750; start = 9,600 + 800 × 0.75 = 10,200; average 10,475. ROE = 500 / 10,475 = 4.77% → closest to 4.7%. B uses unadjusted equity (500/9,800); C adds the full reserve with no tax.

questions.stem: Holding too much inventory LEAST likely results in:
questions.explanation: Excess inventory raises storage/insurance and ties up cash; it LOWERS turnover (bigger denominator).
questions.kr: 과잉재고 → 보관·보험비 ↑, 현금 묶임; 회전율은 '하락'.

questions.stem: Reported inventory (net) is €1,200m and the valuation allowance is €300m. Historical cost is closest to:
questions.explanation: Historical cost = carrying amount + allowance = 1,500.
questions.kr: 취득원가 = 장부가 + 충당금 = 1,500.

questions.stem: An inventory valuation allowance rises from 10% to 20% of gross inventory over two years. This most likely indicates:
questions.explanation: A growing share of inventory impaired → obsolescence warning (Jollof: 13.6% → 22.3%).
questions.kr: 손상 비중 증가 → 진부화 경고(Jollof).

questions.stem: With rising costs and stable quantities, a FIFO company would report under weighted average an inventory turnover that is:
questions.explanation: Weighted average: COGS higher (numerator ↑) and inventory lower (denominator ↓) → turnover higher.
questions.kr: 가중평균: 매출원가 ↑, 재고 ↓ → 회전율 ↑.

questions.stem: Under the same conditions, ROA under weighted average vs FIFO is most likely:

choices.A: higher, because total assets are lower
choices.B: lower, because the decrease in net income outweighs the decrease in assets

questions.explanation: The same absolute change hits NI and assets, but NI is far smaller: €3m/€100m = 3.00% vs €4m/€101m = 3.96%. Numerator effect dominates.
questions.kr: 같은 금액이 순이익·자산에 영향, 순이익이 훨씬 작음 → 분자 효과 우세.

questions.stem: Under the same conditions, debt-to-equity under weighted average vs FIFO is:
questions.explanation: Lower NI → lower retained earnings → lower equity → higher D/E.
questions.kr: 순이익 ↓ → 자본 ↓ → 부채비율 ↑.

questions.stem: Long-term bonds 3,000; other long-term debt 100; current portion of LTD 400; pension liabilities 2,000; equity 5,000. Debt-to-equity using only interest-bearing debt is closest to:
questions.explanation: Debt = 3,000 + 100 + 400 = 3,500 / 5,000 = 0.70. Pensions excluded (B includes them). C drops the current portion.
questions.kr: 부채 = 3,500 / 5,000 = 0.70. 연금 제외(B 포함), C는 유동성 대체분 누락.

questions.stem: If replacement costs were FALLING, a switch from FIFO to weighted average would most likely result in:

choices.A: higher gross margin and higher inventory
choices.B: lower gross margin and lower inventory

questions.explanation: Falling costs: weighted average COGS is LOWER than FIFO (FIFO expenses the older, higher costs) and inventory HIGHER → every rising-cost conclusion reverses; turnover falls.
questions.kr: 원가 하락: 가중평균 매출원가 < FIFO, 재고 ↑ → 상승기 결론 모두 반대, 회전율 ↓.

questions.front: What is capitalised into inventory, what is expensed, and the direction if you get it wrong
questions.back:
IN: purchase price, import duties, freight-in, transit insurance, handling, direct labour, FIXED and variable production overhead. Trade discounts REDUCE cost.
OUT (WSAS): abnormal Waste, Storage (unless needed for production), Admin overhead, Selling (incl. freight-out).
Wrongly capitalising → profit AND inventory both overstated.

questions.front: FIFO vs LIFO vs weighted average in rising and falling prices
questions.back:
Rule: LIFO's COGS and FIFO's EI carry the NEWEST prices.
RISING: FIFO → COGS low, EI high, profit high; LIFO → COGS high, EI low, profit low.
FALLING: everything reverses (GSI: LIFO GP highest).
Weighted average always between; specific ID not necessarily.
Check: COGS + EI = goods available. Weighted avg = total cost ÷ total UNITS available.

questions.front: LIFO vs FIFO with rising costs and stable/rising units — every statement and ratio
questions.back:
IS: COGS ↑; GP, op. income, pre-tax, tax, NI ↓.
BS: inventory, CA, working capital, total assets, RE, equity ↓.
CF: OPERATING CASH FLOW ↑ (lower taxes).
Ratios: current ratio ↓, D/E ↑, profitability ↓, turnover ↑ (deceptive).
FIFO = current values on balance sheet; LIFO = current values on income statement.
Periodic = perpetual for specific ID and FIFO only.

questions.front: The four conversion lines (inventory, COGS, NI, equity)
questions.back:
Reserve = FIFO inv − LIFO inv.
FIFO inventory = LIFO inventory + reserve (LEVEL).
FIFO COGS = LIFO COGS − (end reserve − begin reserve) (CHANGE; falling reserve → ADD).
FIFO NI = LIFO NI + Δreserve × (1 − t).
FIFO equity = LIFO equity + reserve × (1 − t); reserve × t = deferred tax LIABILITY (not cash).

questions.front: What it is, the signal, the profit calc, why unsustainable
questions.back:
Units sold > units bought → old cheap layers into COGS → one-time profit.
Signal: DECLINE in the LIFO reserve.
Causes: supplier strike, recession, deliberate manipulation.
Profit = units liquidated × (current cost − old layer cost). RF: 1,000 × (115 − 100) = 15,000.
With a falling reserve LIFO looks MORE profitable and FIFO CFO is HIGHER.

questions.front: IFRS vs US GAAP write-down and reversal rules, market, ratio effects
questions.back:
IFRS: lower of cost and NRV; reversal REQUIRED, capped at original write-down, as a reduction of COGS.
US GAAP: lower of cost or NRV; LIFO/retail → lower of cost or MARKET (replacement cost; ceiling NRV; floor NRV − normal margin = MIDDLE value); NO reversals.
Agri/forest/mineral producers, broker-traders: fair value less costs to sell, changes in P&L.
Write-down: profitability, liquidity, solvency ↓; ACTIVITY (turnover) ↑. LIFO firms write down less.

questions.front: Inventory ratios, the turnover diagnosis, method changes
questions.back:
Turnover = COGS ÷ average inventory; days = 365 ÷ turnover (may use ending inventory); GM = GP ÷ sales.
High turnover: efficient (few write-downs, sales growth ≥ industry) OR too little inventory (slow sales growth) OR write-downs. Low: slow/obsolete.
Method change: retrospective (restate; earlier effect → opening RE) EXCEPT US GAAP change TO LIFO = prospective (old carrying amount = first layer).
To LIFO = lower tax; from LIFO = higher profit.
